prompt.en: In the note, the nearness of the Hour means that once prophethood has closed with the Prophet, nothing is left to await but the Resurrection.

explanation.en: Qummi glosses the opening words to mean that, because prophethood and messengership have ended with the Prophet, nothing is left to come but the Resurrection.

anchor.quote: after the Prophet nothing remains but the Resurrection, since prophethood and messengership have ended

prompt.en: 'No drop of rain descends from the sky except by a counted number and a known weight ...' Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam Ali taught that rain always falls by a fixed number and weight, except the Flood water in Noah's time, which poured down without weight or number.

anchor.quote: No drop of rain descends from the sky except by a counted number and a known weight

prompt.en: According to the essay, what does Tabrisi say sets this book apart from every other revealed book?

options.en: It alone is recited in full from memory
It records the fates of all the vanished nations
It was sent down complete on a single night
It can be grasped without any admonishment

explanation.en: The essay cites Tabrisi's point that, unlike any other revealed scripture, the Quran alone is recited in full from memory.

anchor.quote: no revealed book but this one is recited in full from memory

prompt.en: The surah then recalls the vanished nations, in what Tabatabai hears as a tone of ____.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai hears the retelling of the destroyed nations in a tone of reproach, not neutral narration.

anchor.quote: The surah then recalls the vanished nations, in what Tabatabai hears as a tone of reproach

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what do the two traditions agree on in reading this passage?

options.en: The moon will split only at the coming Hour
The splitting is a parable rather than a real event
The Quraysh never demanded any sign from the Prophet
Both relate the moon's splitting as a past miracle at Mecca

explanation.en: The perspectives say both traditions read the plain sense alike and relate the splitting of the moon as a past miracle worked at Mecca.

anchor.quote: both relate the splitting of the moon as a past miracle worked at Mecca

prompt.en: "God never destroys a people until He has first sent them messengers to establish the proof against them." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about Thamud's destruction, Imam al-Sadiq states the principle that God never ruins a people until He has sent them messengers to establish the proof, then sent them Salih.

anchor.quote: God never destroys a people until He has first sent them messengers to establish the proof against them

prompt.en: According to the passage, what objection did Thamud raise against Salih?

options.en: He brought them no sign or miracle
They would not follow a lone man from among themselves
He forbade them from sharing their water
He came from a people far away

explanation.en: The essay reports that Thamud objected to following a lone man from among themselves, and branded Salih a self-conceited liar rather than heed his warning.

anchor.quote: they would not follow a lone man from among themselves and branding him a self-conceited liar

prompt.en: The companion they call is ____, the man who hamstrung the she-camel.

explanation.en: The note identifies the companion whom Thamud called, in verse 29, as Qudar, the man who took the blade and hamstrung the she-camel.

anchor.quote: The companion they call is Qudar, the man who hamstrung the she-camel

prompt.en: In the narration about Lot's guests, how were his people's eyes blotted out?

options.en: The rain of stones struck them blind
The single Cry took their sight
Gabriel gestured toward them with his finger

explanation.en: In the narration, when Lot's people forced their way in, Gabriel told Lot to admit them, then gestured with his finger and their eyes were gone.

anchor.quote: Gabriel gestured toward them with his finger and their eyes were gone

prompt.en: In this passage the refrain about the Quran being made simple follows only the story of Thamud, not that of Lot.

explanation.en: The refrain closes both stories, verse 32 after Thamud and verse 40 after Lot; the essay notes it recurs in every story to warn that denying any messenger draws punishment.

anchor.quote: this refrain recurs in every story to press home that denying any messenger draws down the punishment

prompt.en: "In the inner meaning of the Quran, they denied the successors, all of them." Who said this about those who denied God's signs?

explanation.en: Asked about 'They denied all Our signs,' Imam al-Baqir gave its inner meaning: that these deniers rejected the successors, every one of them.

anchor.quote: in the inner meaning of the Quran, they denied the successors, all of them

prompt.en: In Hell there is a valley for the ____ called Saqar.

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq described Saqar as a valley in Hell set apart for the arrogant, so fierce that its own breath, once loosed, set Hell ablaze.

anchor.quote: In Hell there is a valley for the arrogant called Saqar

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what do both readings of verse 49 agree it was turned against?

options.en: The Qadariyya, who deny God's decree
Pharaoh's clan, who denied all the signs
The guilty, steeped in error and madness

explanation.en: Both readings agree verse 49 was turned against the Qadariyya, who deny that God decrees and writes things before He creates them.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai agrees the verse was turned against the Qadariyya who deny that decree

prompt.en: According to the passage, every deed, large or small, already stands written in the books kept by the angels.

explanation.en: The essay stresses that nothing escapes record: every deed, small and great, already stands written in the angels' books, so this is true.

anchor.quote: Every deed, small and great, already stands recorded in the angels' books

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does the surah end after recounting the ruined nations?

options.en: The guilty dragged on their faces into the Fire
The confederate league routed and turned to flee
Pharaoh's clan seized by the Almighty and Omnipotent
The Godwary amid gardens and streams before an omnipotent King

explanation.en: After the ruined nations and the Fire, the essay says the surah closes by turning to the Godwary, placing them in gardens and streams before an omnipotent King.

anchor.quote: the surah ends by turning to the Godwary: gardens and running water, a seat of truth before an omnipotent King
